newsitem.title: USA: Estrada hires Deborah Jones to run Houston office.
newsitem.headline: Estrada hires Deborah Jones to run Houston office.

text.p: Estrada Hinojosa & Co. has hired Deborah Jones, formerly of Alex. Brown & Sons Inc., to head its Houston office.
"Just when they announced they were shutting down we were looking, and had been talking to her," Robert Estrada, the Dallas-based firm's chairman and chief executive officer, said Monday.
Jones, who joined Estrada Hinojosa as a vice president about a week ago, replaces J. Art Morales, a vice president who left to head the Houston office Samuel A. Ramirez & Co opened in April.
Prior to working in Alex. Brown's Houston public finance office, Jones worked at Ponder & Co in Bedford, Texas.
"She's been in the industry probably about 10 years, just a good, seasoned investment banker," Estrada said.
Jones' hiring comes on the heels of another recent addition to the firm, he said. In April, Carl Despagni joined Estrada's Dallas office as a vice president in trading and underwriting.

Despagni, a 17 to 18-year industry veteran, began his career at Shearson Lehman Brothers, but had been out of the industry for the past two or three years. His return via Estrada Hinojosa is "helping us in boosting our sales capability here," Estrada said.
Another recent development at Estrada Hinojosa involves the company's repurchase of its outstanding preferred stock.

"Back in 1992 when we were a fledgling start-up firm, we entered into an agreement with Morgan Keegan & Co, the big Memphis underwriting firm, where they initially gave us a subordinated loan to boost our capital position," Estrada said.
In 1993, the loan was contractually converted to preferred stock issued to Morgan Keegan.

"So they have been a preferred stock holder of Estrada Hinojosa for about three-and-a-half, four years," Estrada said, adding that if Morgan Keegan had ever decided to convert the stock, it was entitled to about 30 percent equity in Estrada Hinojosa. Instead, the repurchase was completed in late March.
"We bought back the stock we issued to them, which they didn't have to sell us," Estrada said. "It was strictly their option, but we had a very friendly agreement."
That gives Estrada and partner Noe Hinojosa Jr. full control instead of just 70 percent.
"And that's a big milestone for us," Estrada said.
Estrada Hinojosa used funds from last year's earnings to repurchase the stock, but Estrada declined to place a dollar amount on the transaction.
"That's not disclosable yet, but it was a pretty fair price, it was about equal to the 30 percent based on our total assets," he said.
In addition to Dallas and Houston, Estrada Hinojosa has offices in San Antonio, Texas, and Phoenix, Ariz.
